newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks extend gains at midday.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks extend gains at midday.

text.p: Wall Street stocks extended their gains at midday Monday, with the high techs moving up on positive news on global shipments of personal computers and the overall market benefiting from an uptick in bonds.
The Dow industrials were up 44 points at 6782, surprising analysts who had expected a sell-off in Boeing Co to weigh more heavily on the index.
"A lot of pessimism has built up since our run-up," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Chareter Ltd. "As pessimism builds, money is put back to work."
Big Board advances led declining issues by 13 to 10 on volume of about 213 million shares.
The Nasdaq Composite Average was up nine points at 1218.
U.S. Treasuries were higher, with the long bond up 3/32 to yield 7.14 percent.
"The market internals aren't wonderful, but the Big Board is doing okay. A lot of Dow stocks are in the process of breaking out to the upside," Bleier said.
Some analysts said the bounce from three days of weakness was very impressive; they were surprised the market was doing so well.

"I'm surprised at the strength in stocks because bond yields are still high and we are the start of a week full of economic data which could hit bonds again," said Jim Solloway, director of research at Argus Research.
"The stock market is priced at a level that makes it vulnerable to any decline in bond prices," he said.

Referring to the market's strength, he added, "We have a strong economy providing hope for corporate profits. In the first quarter, we were in pretty good shape as far as individual companies are concerned."
He said another interest rate hike when Federal Reserve policy-makers meet May 20 was "already cooked into prices." He said uncertainty about the course of Fed action remained.

"Investors shouldn't worry so much about the next increase," he said. "The question is how many more tightenings will there be before the Fed stops. No one has a good handle on that. I don't think we'll end with just one more increase.
"Until there is greater certainty that the current tightening phase is coming to an end, the market will remain volatile, but in a broad range between 6400/6500-7100."
Techs rallied on news that global unit shipments of personal computers jumped 16 percent in the first quarter from a year earlier, according to International Data Corp.
The research firm said U.S. shipments rose 20 percent, the most of any major region and the best quarterly U.S. growth rate since the end of 1995.

High techs were boosted by the news. Cisco Systems Inc, the most actively traded Nasdaq issue, was up 3/8 at 46-3/4. Intel Corp was up 2-3/8 at 146-1/4. Dell Computer Corp was up 2-1/4 at 80. Sun Microsystems Inc was up 1-1/8 at 28-1/4.
American Express Co was up 2-7/8 at 64.
Hambrecht & Quist said it cut its rating on Nike Inc to hold from buy based on weakness in U.S. markets. Nike shares were down 2-3/4 at 53-1/2.

McDonnell Douglas Corp was off three points at 57-1/2 in sympathy with Boeing Co, which was down 5-3/4 to 96-1/4, analysts said. McDonnell shares have been trading in sync with Boeing's stock since the two aircraft companies announced a proposed merger agreement.
Boeing shares dropped after the company reported lower than expected earnings.
